q: A clerk is formally ordered to hold full additional charge of another post for 30 days. He claims Additional Post Allowance for the month. What is the correct position?

options.A: APA is payable at 10% of his basic pay for the 30 days
options.B: No APA is payable, because the additional charge did not exceed 45 days
options.C: APA is payable at 5% of his basic pay for a spell below 45 days
options.D: APA is payable in full because a formal order was issued

e: APA is admissible only if the duration of the additional charge exceeds 45 days; a 30-day spell earns no APA.

q: An employee holds full additional charge of another post for 52 days. No separate pay attaches to the additional post. Which statement about his APA is correct?

options.A: APA is admissible at 2% of his own basic pay per month
options.B: Only the pay of his own post is payable, as in current charge
options.C: APA is admissible at 10% of his own basic pay per month
options.D: APA is not admissible because the spell is below two months

e: The charge exceeded 45 days, so APA is admissible; where no separate pay attaches to the additional post, it is 10% of own basic pay per month.

q: For 70 days an employee is asked to hold only current charge of a higher post, looking after its day-to-day routine work without discharging its statutory functions. He claims APA. The claim is:

options.A: Admissible at 10% of his basic pay, as the spell exceeded 45 days
options.B: Admissible at 10% of the higher post's pay
options.C: Not admissible; he draws only the pay of his own post
options.D: Admissible for the period beyond 45 days only

e: Current charge covers only routine duties and carries no additional pay; APA requires a formal order for full additional charge.

q: A railway pensioner asks what Dearness Relief he will draw with effect from 1 January 2026. The correct reply is:
e: DR for pensioners is also 60% from 01.01.2026, issued through RBE 36/2026; RBE 34/2026 covers DA for serving employees.

q: A loco pilot and a clerk draw the same basic pay. The loco pilot's DA for the month is visibly higher. The reason is that for running staff DA is calculated on:

options.A: Basic pay plus the 30% pay element of running staff
options.C: Basic pay plus the running allowance actually earned
options.D: Basic pay doubled for the running portion of duty

e: For running staff, DA is calculated on basic pay plus the 30% pay element, so the same basic pay draws higher DA than for stationary staff.

q: An employee's full additional charge of another post lasts exactly 45 days and then ends. His APA claim should be:

options.A: Allowed, because 45 days is the qualifying minimum
options.B: Rejected, because APA requires the additional charge to exceed 45 days
options.C: Allowed at half the monthly rate for the 45th day
options.D: Allowed, because the charge was of a full post

e: The condition is that the duration exceeds 45 days; a spell of exactly 45 days does not cross the gate.

q: A teacher is given charge of the school library as a specified extra duty in addition to his normal work, and claims Additional Post Allowance. The correct treatment is:

options.A: APA at 10% of basic pay is payable for the library charge
options.B: No allowance of any kind can be paid for extra duties
options.C: Additional Allowance for running staff is payable instead
options.D: The claim is not APA; specified extra duties are covered by Extra Work Allowance at 2% of basic pay

e: APA compensates full additional charge of another post. Specified extra duties such as library charge fall under Extra Work Allowance at 2% of basic pay.

q:
Consider the following statements about the recent DA ladder:
I. DA was 50% with effect from January 2024.
II. DA was 55% with effect from July 2024.
III. DA is 60% with effect from 1 January 2026.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: The ladder is 50% (Jan 2024), 53% (Jul 2024), 55% (Jan 2025), 58% (Jul 2025) and 60% (Jan 2026); statement II misplaces 55%.

q:
Consider the following statements about Additional Post Allowance:
I. APA replaced the old Dual Charge Allowance.
II. APA is admissible for an additional charge of 30 days.
III. An employee holding only current charge of a post draws APA at 10% of basic pay.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Only statement I is correct. APA needs a spell exceeding 45 days, and current charge draws no additional pay at all.

q:
Consider the following statements about Dearness Allowance:
I. DA is a distinct element of pay and is not merged with basic pay.
II. Fractions of 50 paise and above in DA are rounded up to the next rupee.
III. The Night Duty Allowance formula and Transport Allowance both take DA into account.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: All three are correct: DA is a distinct element, the 50-paise rounding rule applies, Transport Allowance carries DA and the NDA rate uses (Basic Pay + DA).

q: What is the rate of Dearness Allowance for railway employees with effect from 1 January 2026?
e: DA is 60% of basic pay w.e.f. 01.01.2026; 58% was the July 2025 rate.

q: Dearness Allowance at 60% with effect from 1 January 2026 was issued through which Railway Board circular?
e: RBE 34/2026 covers DA for employees; RBE 36/2026 covers Dearness Relief for pensioners.

q: Dearness Relief for railway pensioners at 60% with effect from 1 January 2026 was issued through:
e: DR is also 60% from 01.01.2026, under RBE 36/2026.

q: What was the rate of Dearness Allowance with effect from July 2025, immediately before the January 2026 revision?
e: The ladder runs 55% (Jan 2025) to 58% (Jul 2025) to 60% (Jan 2026).

q: Additional Post Allowance was introduced, replacing Dual Charge Allowance, through:
e: APA replaced the old Dual Charge Allowance under RBE 128/2018.

q: Where no separate pay attaches to the additional post, Additional Post Allowance is payable at:

options.A: 2% of the employee's own basic pay per month
options.B: 20% of the employee's own basic pay per month
options.C: 10% of the employee's own basic pay per month

e: In that situation APA is 10% of own basic pay per month; 2% is the Extra Work Allowance rate.

q: Additional Post Allowance becomes admissible only when the period of additional charge:
e: The bank-tested gate is that the additional charge must exceed 45 days.

q: An employee draws basic pay of Rs 50,000 in January 2026. His Dearness Allowance for the month is:
e: DA at 60% of Rs 50,000 is Rs 30,000.

q: An employee in Level 6 draws basic pay of Rs 44,900. DA payable at the January 2026 rate is:
e: DA at 60% of Rs 44,900 is Rs 26,940.

q: A running staff employee draws basic pay of Rs 40,000. His DA for January 2026, calculated on basic pay plus the 30% pay element, is:
e: The DA base is 40,000 + 12,000 = 52,000, and 60% of that is Rs 31,200.

q: A railway pensioner draws a basic pension of Rs 35,000. Dearness Relief payable from January 2026 is:
e: DR at 60% of Rs 35,000 is Rs 21,000.

q: An employee with basic pay of Rs 62,000 holds full additional charge of another post for 60 days, and no separate pay attaches to that post. His APA per month is:

options.D: Nil, as the spell is too short

e: The spell exceeds 45 days, so APA is 10% of Rs 62,000 = Rs 6,200 per month.

q: An employee with basic pay of Rs 53,100 holds full additional charge of a post of the same level for 58 days. His APA per month is:
e: For a same-level additional post, APA is 10% of present basic pay: 10% of Rs 53,100 = Rs 5,310.

q: An employee draws basic pay of Rs 70,000. The increase in his monthly DA when the rate rose from 55% (January 2025) to 60% (January 2026) is:
e: DA rose from Rs 38,500 at 55% to Rs 42,000 at 60%, an increase of Rs 3,500.

q: An employee draws basic pay of Rs 39,800 in January 2026. His basic pay plus DA for the month totals:
e: DA is Rs 23,880, so basic pay plus DA is 39,800 + 23,880 = Rs 63,680.

q: An employee with basic pay of Rs 48,000 holds full additional charge, with no separate pay attached to the additional post, for three full months. The total APA payable for the three months is:
e: APA is Rs 4,800 per month, so three months give Rs 14,400.

q: An employee draws basic pay of Rs 66,700. DA payable at the rate in force from 1 January 2026 is:
e: DA at 60% of Rs 66,700 is Rs 40,020.

q: Which of the following statements about Dearness Allowance is NOT correct?

options.A: DA is 60% of basic pay with effect from 1 January 2026
options.B: DA is revised every January and July with the cost of living
options.C: DA is merged with basic pay and loses its separate identity
options.D: For running staff, DA is calculated on basic pay plus the 30% pay element

e: DA remains a distinct element of pay; it is not merged with basic pay. The other statements are correct.

q: Which of the following statements about Additional Post Allowance is NOT correct?

options.A: APA replaced the old Dual Charge Allowance
options.B: APA requires a formal order for full additional charge of another post
options.C: Where no separate pay attaches to the additional post, APA is 10% of own basic pay per month
options.D: APA is admissible even where the additional charge lasts only 20 days

e: APA is admissible only if the additional charge exceeds 45 days, so a 20-day spell earns nothing.

q: Which of the following statements about current charge is NOT correct?

options.A: An employee holding current charge of a higher post draws APA at 10% of his basic pay
options.B: Current charge means looking after only the day-to-day routine duties of a post
options.C: An employee on current charge does not discharge the statutory functions of that post
options.D: APA requires full additional charge, not mere current charge

e: Current charge carries no additional pay; the employee draws only the pay of his own post.

q: Which of the following statements about the DA ladder is NOT correct?

options.A: DA was 50% with effect from January 2024
options.B: DA was 53% with effect from January 2025
options.C: DA was 58% with effect from July 2025
options.D: DA is 60% with effect from January 2026

e: 53% was the July 2024 rate; January 2025 brought 55%.

q: Which of the following statements is NOT correct?

options.A: Additional Allowance is the renamed Special Running Staff Allowance
options.B: Extra Work Allowance is paid at 2% of basic pay per month
options.C: Additional Post Allowance is the running staff allowance paid at Rs 750, Rs 1,125 or Rs 2,250 per month
options.D: Additional Post Allowance compensates full additional charge of another post

e: The Rs 750/1,125/2,250 monthly figures belong to Additional Allowance for running staff, not to APA.

q:
Assertion (A): Additional Post Allowance is admissible only if the additional charge exceeds 45 days.
Reason (R): Additional Post Allowance replaced the old Dual Charge Allowance under RBE 128/2018.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R correctly explains A
options.B: Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D: A is false but R is true

e: Both statements are true, but the replacement of Dual Charge Allowance does not explain the 45-day condition.

q:
Assertion (A): An employee holding current charge of a higher post is entitled to Additional Post Allowance at 10% of his basic pay.
Reason (R): Current charge covers only the day-to-day routine duties of the post and not its statutory functions.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R correctly explains A
options.B: Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D: A is false but R is true

e: A is false because current charge draws no additional pay; R is true and states what current charge means.

q:
Assertion (A): For running staff, DA is calculated on basic pay plus a 30% pay element.
Reason (R): A 30% pay element forms part of the pay structure of running staff and is taken into account for DA and retirement benefits.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R correctly explains A
options.B: Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D: A is false but R is true

e: Both are true, and R explains why the DA base of running staff is higher than basic pay alone.
